text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Hiroshi Yasuda, the governor of the Export-Import Bank of Japan, told Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar that the bank was considering extending an unspecified loan to Slovakia. If provided, the loan would be the Exim bank's third credit facility for Slovakia.
- Top Japanese government officials said Tokyo would support Slovakia's attempt to become a full member of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

- The Transport Ministry has repeatedly rejected as unacceptable the Czech proposal to move a planned motorway connection between the Baltic sea and Vienna from Slovak territory to the eastern part of the Czech Republic.
- The Czech-Slovak trade in the first two month of this year showed a Slovak deficit of 3.7 billion crowns, according to Czech statistical data.
NARODNA OBRODA - The government holds its regular session on Tuesday with no major economic items on the preliminary agenda.

- Trade unions of the coal mining industry are demanding a 30 percent increase in wages this year, while employers are offering a maximum six percent. The unions said miners were likely to start protest actions if the two sides do not reach an agreement in the next round of talks, scheduled for April 2.

SME - Jan Slota, leader of the junior coalition party, the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), will attend a congress of the extreme-right French National Front, led by Jean-Marie Le Pen, scheduled for next weekend.
- Slota is expected to invite Le Pen to visit Slovakia.

PRAVDA - Slovak theatres will on Wednesday stop their protest strike, called over a month ago against the state interference in the culture. But the actors said they would remain on strike alert until state authorities are willing to open a dialogue with them over the problems in the culture.
